newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pension fund PGGM still positive on Dutch shares.
newsitem.headline: Pension fund PGGM still positive on Dutch shares.

text.p: PGGM, the second largest pension fund in the Netherlands, said on Tuesday it would likely retain an overweight position in the Dutch sharemarket this year.
Financial controller Peter van den Berg said the health sector fund currently had 28 percent of its equities portfolio invested in Dutch equities, compared with its target level of 21 percent.
Asked after a news conference on PGGM's 1996 results how the exposure to Dutch shares would change over the rest of 1997, he said: "We will not be moving it very much."
"At the moment we are very positive on our own country," Van den Berg told Reuters.
At December 31, PGGM had 30.9 billion guilders invested in equities, or 47 percent of its total investment portfolio of 65.9 billion guilders.
PGGM realised a return of 15.9 percent on its investments in 1996, up from 13.1 percent in 1995, mainly due to the high percentage of shares within its portfolio.
Shares yielded a 26 percent return, compared to 8.4 percent from fixed interest investments and 10.1 percent from property.
The Dutch sharemarket rose 34 percent in 1996.
